answers_by_date.answer: Equal access to all types of social security protections after some period of time
answers_by_date.basis: Ley 22.439 arts. 26-29 let permanent, temporary and authorised residents work 'gozando de la protección de las leyes que rigen la materia'. The contributory pension system (Ley 24.241, art. 2 compulsory membership, art. 19 PBU) makes no distinction by nationality. Non-contributory old-age and disability pensions required foreigners to prove 20 years' continuous residence (Decreto 432/97, Anexo I, 1.e). So the answer is the same as in 2020. I found no practice evidence I could read for this period (CELS 2002-03 report located but not readable), so the rating is carried over.

answers_by_date.answer: Equal access to all types of social security protections after some period of time
answers_by_date.basis: Ley 25.871 (from January 2004) art. 6 promises immigrants equal access to 'seguridad social'. Contributory schemes stay nationality-neutral. Decreto 582/2003 (Aug 2003) raised the residence requirement for foreigners claiming the non-contributory old-age pension to 40 years, while the disability pension kept 20 years. Access is therefore still equal only after a period of residence. I could read no practice evidence for this period, so the rating is carried over.

answers_by_date.answer: Equal access to all types of social security protections after some period of time
answers_by_date.basis: Same statutes, plus three changes. Ley 26.202 approved the ICRMW, in force for Argentina from 2007; its art. 27 gives equal social-security treatment 'en la medida en que cumplan los requisitos previstos en la legislación'. Decreto 1602/2009 (Nov 2009) created the AUH child allowance, with 3 years' legal residence required for non-nationals (Ley 24.714 art. 14 ter). The CSJN's Reyes Aguilera ruling (4 Sept 2007) struck down the 20-year rule only for the claimant. The CMW in 2011 documented excessive residence requirements of 3/15/20/40 years still being applied after that ruling, which supports 'Sometimes'.

answers_by_date.answer: Equal access to all types of social security protections after some period of time
answers_by_date.basis: Decreto 616/2010 art. 6 (May 2010) tells authorities to guarantee migrants' access to social security 'en igualdad de condiciones con los nacionales'. The residence requirements for non-contributory benefits and the AUH remained. Practice evidence is the CMW 2011 findings, which have not been corrected. Between 2015 and 2020 the PUAM (Ley 27.260, July 2016) added a 20-year residence rule for foreigners, and the CMW repeated its recommendation in 2019, which is consistent with the 2020 answer.

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been right protections both in 2000 and 2020 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

answers.starting_answer_concern: The 2023 citation leans on Ley 24.241 art. 19 (30 years of contributions), but that rule applies to nationals too. The real basis for 'after some period of time' is the residence requirements for non-contributory benefits: Decreto 432/97 (20 years), Decreto 582/2003 (40 years), AUH (3 years) and PUAM (20 years). Contributory protections are immediate and equal. The answer holds on those grounds.
answers.notes: Protection answers rest on statutes and decrees. Reyes Aguilera was used only as practice evidence: I did not read it in full, it was a split decision, and its effect was confined to the claimant. The ICRMW (Ley 26.202) is directly applicable under art. 75 inc. 22, but its art. 27 defers to national eligibility requirements. Ley 25.871 art. 6 was later amended by DNU 366/2025 (after 2020).

answers_by_date.answer: Equal access to all types of unemployment benefits after a duration of stay
answers_by_date.basis: Ley 24.013 Title IV (arts. 111-118, in force since Dec 1991) covers workers under the LCT with no distinction by nationality. Benefits depend on contributions to the Fondo Nacional del Empleo. Ley 22.439 arts. 26-27 let authorised residents work with the protection of labour laws, while art. 30 barred irregular migrants from working. The answer is kept as in 2020. I found no practice evidence on migrants' access to unemployment benefits for this period, so the rating is carried over.

answers_by_date.answer: Equal access to all types of unemployment benefits after a duration of stay
answers_by_date.basis: Ley 25.871 art. 6 (from January 2004) adds equal access to 'trabajo, empleo y seguridad social'. Ley 24.013 is unchanged. I found no practice evidence, so the rating is carried over (low confidence).

answers_by_date.answer: Equal access to all types of unemployment benefits after a duration of stay
answers_by_date.basis: Decreto 267/2006 (BO 13-03-2006) replaced art. 113 c) (now 6 months of contributions in the last 3 years) and art. 117 (benefit duration scales with contribution period), without touching nationality. ICRMW art. 54(1)(b), through Ley 26.202 (in force 2007), adds equal treatment in unemployment benefits. I found no migrant-specific practice evidence, so the rating is carried over.

answers_by_date.answer: Equal access to all types of unemployment benefits after a duration of stay
answers_by_date.basis: Same provisions; Decreto 616/2010 art. 6 adds the equal-access duty for employment and social security. Up to 2020 nothing changed in the text bearing on migrants. The only practice signal is the general CMW 2011 concern about informality and documentation barriers; I found nothing specific to unemployment benefits.

answers.sourcing_note: I read Ley 24.013's consolidated text with its amendment notes, part of InfoLEG's 'normas que modifican' list, the original and current Ley 25.871, Ley 22.439 and Ley 26.202. The pre-2006 wording of art. 113 c) was not read. I found no practice evidence specific to migrants' unemployment benefits for any date, and PDF reports could not be opened.
answers.starting_answer_concern: Ley 24.013 arts. 111-118 make no distinction by nationality or length of residence. The qualifying period is a contribution period (6 months in 3 years) that applies equally to nationals, and ICRMW art. 54 (Ley 26.202) guarantees equal treatment. On the text, 'Yes, immediate equal access to all types of unemployment benefits' looks more accurate. The 'Rarely' rating has no documented evidence behind it. The 2023 citation also mislabels Ley 24.013 as the 'Work Contract Act' (it is the Ley Nacional de Empleo; the LCT is Ley 20.744).
answers.notes: No rulings relied on. Decreto 90/2023 (after 2020) rewrote art. 112's first paragraph to cover domestic workers under Ley 26.844; it does not bear on 2000-2020. The ratings for past dates are carried over from the starting answer for lack of practice evidence.
